description: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) of five different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, and ROME—across varying co-occurrence numbers, with the x-axis representing the co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 1000, and the y-axis showing accuracy in percentage from 60% to 80%. The Base method, represented by a black line with circular markers, starts at approximately 62% accuracy at a co-occurrence number of 1 and increases steadily to about 67% at a co-occurrence number of 1000. The MEND method, shown with a brown line and diamond markers, begins at around 66% and rises to approximately 76% at the highest co-occurrence number. The FT method, depicted with a blue line and triangle markers, starts at about 63% and increases to roughly 68% at the end of the range. The MEMIT method, represented by a purple line with pentagon markers, begins at approximately 66% and climbs to about 77% at the highest co-occurrence number. The ROME method, shown with a green line and square markers, starts at around 74% and increases to approximately 78% at the highest co-occurrence number. Overall, the ROME method consistently achieves the highest accuracy across all co-occurrence numbers, while the Base method shows the lowest accuracy throughout the range.
